name: Visually Hidden
summary: One class that takes text off the screen and leaves it in the accessibility tree — the difference between hiding something from sight and hiding it from everyone.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page. Example 4 is four identical-looking buttons where three have no accessible name at all — inspect the accessibility tree, or listen to them.

contract.useWhen: Text for screen readers only, in nine declarations that all matter.
failureModes: display:none, visibility:hidden or the hidden attribute — all three leave the tree
visibility:hidden keeping its layout box, so the labeled button is stretched by text nobody reads
width and height at 0 rather than 1px, which can drop out of the accessibility tree
no white-space:nowrap, so the text wraps inside 1px and is read letter by letter
aria-label as a shorter spelling: it needs a naming role, replaces the whole name (SC 2.5.3), and is invisible to translation
:focus instead of :focus-within on the focusable variant, when the focusable thing is inside
